# .: everything in one file

> Sourdough makes a new Wayne State app with the stack already wired in: SESAME sign-in, HELMET runtime baseline, PROCTOR checks, WayneUI and a Citadel release script. One PHP command, every operating system.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/README.md

A starter you feed: `sourdough new` makes a Wayne State app with the stack already wired in.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Every loaf gets proofed before it ships.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page you can open in a browser or serve from `site/`.

On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

This repository is published from Wayne State University's internal GitLab and mirrored here. Changes land there first; Wayne State developers open issues and merge requests on the internal project.

Sourdough is the app starter for the WSU stack. One command scaffolds a new app with SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), PROCTOR (checks), and the Preflight CI components already in place. It is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

### Install

```
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
```

Or scaffold without installing, with `composer create-project waynestate/sourdough`.

### Usage

```
sourdough new [dir] [options]
```

`dir` is the directory to create the app in. It is required unless you use `--describe`.

Options:

- `--raw` use the raw PHP base
- `--laravel` use the Laravel base
- `--vue` add a Vue front end
- `--inertia` use Inertia/Vue (implies `--laravel`)
- `--sail` use Laravel Sail for the local runtime (Laravel paths)
- `--docker` use a Docker image for the local runtime (Laravel paths)
- `--dry-run` print the plan and write nothing
- `--name` app name (default: the basename of ``)
- `--no-input` never prompt (Sourdough 0.1 has no prompts)
- `--json` with `--dry-run`, print the plan as JSON
- `--describe ""` describe what the app does; a model plans it (needs the `SOURDOUGH_LLM_*` env vars)
- `--plan-only` with `--describe`, print the plan as JSON and write nothing
- `--plan ` a ready-made plan file (JSON matching `resources/plan.schema.json`)
- `--playbook` require `waynestate/playbook` in the generated app: adds the VCS repository and the package to `require`
- `--no-playbook` skip the Playbook wiring (no `suggest`, no `.env.example` block, no README section)

Exit codes: `0` done, `1` refused (invalid flags, non-empty target, not available, model gave up), `2` tool error.

By default the generated app suggests `waynestate/playbook` (WSU's private shared-values package on git.wayne.edu), lists its seven setting names in `.env.example`, and documents how to fetch them in a "WSU values (PLAYBOOK)" README section; the command prints a hint line pointing at it after generation. `--playbook` additionally adds the VCS repository and requires the package; `--no-playbook` skips all of it. The two flags together are refused with exit `1`.

The app name (from `--name`, from the plan, or from the basename of ``) must start with a letter or number and use only letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores, at most 63 characters; anything else is refused before anything is written.

### Permutations

| Flags | Permutation |
|---|---|
| (none) or `--raw` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path |
| `--raw --vue` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON |
| `--laravel` | Laravel + Blade |
| `--laravel --vue` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands |
| `--laravel --inertia` (or `--inertia`) | Laravel + Inertia/Vue |

Only `--raw` generates in 0.1. The other permutations print the plan and exit `1` with "not available in this release"; later steps add them.

### Describe a plan

Instead of choosing flags, describe what the app does and let a model plan it:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments"
```

Sourdough asks an OpenAI-compatible model for a plan, validates it against `resources/plan.schema.json`, and prints it. The model kneads the dough, but you decide when the loaf is ready to bake: if the answer is not valid JSON, does not match the schema, or the model gives up after one retry, Sourdough refuses with a message pointing you to `--plan=` (exit `1`). You write the plan yourself and pass it in.

To see the plan as JSON without writing anything:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments" --plan-only
```

Generation from a plan is not built yet in 0.1. Save the plan to a file and pass it with `--plan`:

```
sourdough new my-app --plan plan.json
```

`--plan` reads the file, validates it against the schema, and continues the normal generation flow using the plan's permutation and name.

#### Model configuration

`--describe` needs three environment variables (no defaults, no key in code):

- `SOURDOUGH_LLM_BASE_URL` the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including the API path (usually `/v1`)
- `SOURDOUGH_LLM_API_KEY` the API key
- `SOURDOUGH_LLM_MODEL` the model name

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works: a hosted API, a local server, or WarriorGPT. Sourdough does not care about the hostname; it only needs the base URL, key, and model.

A plan is a small JSON object:

```json
{
    "permutation": "raw",
    "parts": ["sesame", "helmet"],
    "name": "my-app",
    "models": [
        {
            "name": "Post",
            "fields": [
                { "name": "title", "type": "string" },
                { "name": "body", "type": "text" }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "pages": ["/", "/posts"]
}
```

`permutation`, `parts`, and `name` are required; `models` and `pages` are optional. `parts` is a subset of `sesame`, `helmet`, `proctor`, and `preflight`.

### The manifest

Every app Sourdough generates carries a `.sourdough/manifest.json` recording what was generated: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers you chose, and a sha256 hash of every file, each marked `managed` (Sourdough owns it and will update it) or `seeded` (Sourdough wrote it once and you own it now: `.env.example` and `README.md`).

The manifest is the starter's memory: it remembers what went into the loaf, so `feed` knows what to refresh and what to leave to rise on its own. A later `sourdough feed` reads it to bring template updates into your app without clobbering what you've changed.

Until `feed` ships, `sourdough manifest --check` is the gate. Run it in your app to list the managed files that have drifted from the manifest:

```
sourdough manifest --check
```

Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` a managed file changed or is missing, `2` tool error (no manifest, or no `--check`). Seeded files are never reported. They're yours.

Commit the manifest. It's the record that keeps `feed` honest.

The deploy files in your app (`build.sh`, `scripts/release.sh`, the `.squire/` config, and their friends) come from Squire's exported copy, checked into this repository at `templates/squire/`. Squire owns them; Sourdough installs them as-is and records them in the manifest, so you never edit them by hand. To refresh them, run `composer squire-copy:sync`, which rewrites the copy from the installed `waynestate/squire` package, then verify it with `composer squire-copy:check` (part of `composer ci`).

### Testing

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

From the repo root:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer validate --strict
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli php bin/sourdough new /tmp/demo --dry-run
```

### CI

Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner.

Wayne State's app starters

## Sourdough

Feed it and it grows.

![Sourdough mark: a starter jar whose starter has risen into a dome, well above the gold band that marks where it began](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/brand/sourdough-avatar-512.png)

Hungry. It has not been fed yet today.

One command makes a new Wayne State app with the stack already wired in. SESAME signs people in, HELMET sets the runtime baseline, PROCTOR checks the code, WayneUI draws the page, and a Citadel release script ships it. One PHP command, so it bakes the same on Windows, macOS and Linux.

The whole recipe

```
$ composer global require waynestate/sourdough
$ sourdough new my-app
```

**Want every piece already joined? Start from [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/).** Use Sourdough when you want a smaller raw PHP app with SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and Preflight already wired in.

[Start baking](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/#start-title) [See the five loaves](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/#loaves-title)

Proofing log

### The proof

What goes into the tub when you run `sourdough new`.

1. 08:00 **Mix.** `sourdough new` picks the shape: raw PHP, or Laravel, with or without Vue.
2. 08:20 **Flour: WayneUI.** The interface, from WayneUI's standalone PHP path.
3. 08:40 **Water: SESAME.** Sign-in. A fake driver locally, CAS in production.
4. 09:00 **Salt: HELMET.** Security headers, a hardened session, and `/up` for the load balancer.
5. 10:30 **Levain: PROCTOR.** The checks, with Preflight's CI components and a Citadel release script that runs them.
6. 13:00 **Doubled.** Well past the gold band. A label goes on: `.sourdough/manifest.json`.
7. 14:00 **Divide and shape.** One starter, five loaves.

On the cooling rack

### Five loaves, one starter

Every shape a Wayne State app can take. The raw PHP boule is out of the oven in 0.1; the other four are still proofing. Score a loaf to see what's baked in.

Country boule

#### Raw PHP

Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path. No framework, no build.

Out of the oven · 0.1

`sourdough new my-app --raw`

The crumb

- `public/index.php` HELMET boots first, then SESAME signs you in
- `composer.json` helmet and sesame, with proctor for dev
- `.gitlab-ci.yml` Preflight components: PROCTOR, tests on PHP 8.3 to 8.5, audit
- `deployments/release.sh` and `release.ps1` the Citadel release script
- `.env.example` and `README.md` seeded: yours from day one
- `.sourdough/manifest.json` the label on the jar

Bâtard

#### Raw PHP + Vue

A Vue single-page app over JSON, on raw PHP.

Coming soon

The crumb

Cut too early: still dough in the middle. The bake lands in a later release.

Baguette

#### Laravel + Blade

The classic Wayne State shape: Laravel with Blade views.

Coming soon

The crumb

Planned on Laravel's own installer, with the same SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and WayneUI wired in. Still proofing.

Seeded loaf

#### Laravel + Blade + Vue islands

Blade pages with Vue islands, like seeds in the crust.

Coming soon

The crumb

The seeds are counted, the oven isn't hot yet. Coming in a later release.

Tin loaf

#### Laravel + Inertia/Vue

Inertia and Vue: the whole app baked in one tin.

Coming soon

The crumb

Want this one already baked? [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) is the Inertia/Vue loaf, finished and sliced: `composer create-project waynestate/weld my-app`.

Not sure yet? `sourdough new my-app --dry-run` prints the plan and writes nothing. It works with any shape's flags, so you can read a loaf's plan before it bakes.

Recipe card No. 1

### What's baked in

Baker's percentages, roughly. The parts are libraries, so they update with `composer update`; only the glue lives in the template.

**The parts of the stack in every Sourdough app, as ingredients**

| Ingredient | Part | What it does in your app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100% Flour | [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/) | The interface: WayneUI's standalone PHP file, fetched once into `public/`. |
| 75% Water | [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/) | Sign-in. The fake driver in development; the cas driver in production, with `SESAME_CAS_URL` and `SESAME_SERVICE_URL`. |
| 2% Salt | [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/) | The runtime baseline: security headers, session cookie flags, trusted proxies from `HELMET_PROXIES`, and `/up` answering `200 ok`. |
| 20% Levain | [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) | The checks. The release script runs `vendor/bin/proctor check` before anything ships. |
| 1 Oven | [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/) | CI from `.gitlab-ci.yml`: PROCTOR, tests on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, and a Composer audit. |
| 1 Basket | Release script | `deployments/release.sh` runs on Citadel at release time; `release.ps1` is its Windows twin. Off Citadel, the same env vars work on OpenShift, Coolify or raw Docker. |

Bake at `php -S localhost:8000 -t public` until golden.

Pinned above the bench

### Feeding schedule

A starter you never feed goes flat. Every app Sourdough makes carries `.sourdough/manifest.json`: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers you chose, and a sha256 of every file. It's how the starter remembers what went into the loaf.

1. Bake day
   `sourdough new my-app`
   Makes the app and writes the manifest. Commit it: it's the record that keeps feeding honest.
2. Every day, in CI
   `sourdough manifest --check`
   Is it still alive? Lists every managed file that drifted from the manifest.
   - **0**: clean
   - **1**: a managed file changed or is missing
   - **2**: no manifest, or no `--check`
3. Feeding
   sourdough feed coming soon
   Brings template updates into your app without clobbering what you changed.

#### Managed we keep feeding these

- `public/index.php`
- `composer.json`
- `.gitlab-ci.yml`
- `deployments/`
- `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`

#### Seeded written once, yours now

- `.env.example`
- `README.md`

Seeded files are never reported. They're yours to knead.

Quick start

### Your first loaf

Sourdough is one PHP command, so the steps match on every system; only the shell changes. You need PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer.

**Windows**

PowerShell

```
# 1. Get the starter
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
# 2. Bake the app
sourdough new my-app
cd my-app
# 3. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once
curl.exe -o public/wayne-ui.php https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/wayne-ui/-/raw/main/php/standalone/wayne-ui.php
# 4. Install and serve
composer install
php -S localhost:8000 -t public
```

**macOS**

Terminal (zsh)

```
# 1. Get the starter
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
# 2. Bake the app
sourdough new my-app
cd my-app
# 3. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once
curl -o public/wayne-ui.php https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/wayne-ui/-/raw/main/php/standalone/wayne-ui.php
# 4. Install and serve
composer install
php -S localhost:8000 -t public
```

**Linux**

bash

```
# 1. Get the starter
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
# 2. Bake the app
sourdough new my-app
cd my-app
# 3. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once
curl -o public/wayne-ui.php https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/wayne-ui/-/raw/main/php/standalone/wayne-ui.php
# 4. Install and serve
composer install
php -S localhost:8000 -t public
```

**`sourdough` not found?** Add the folder that `composer global config bin-dir --absolute` prints to your PATH. Then open `http://localhost:8000`: locally the app signs in with SESAME's fake driver.

Hand it to your agent

### Recipes for your agent

Two cards, ready for the coding agent you already use. Copy one, or run it straight in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each one says what is in the tub, what the agent may not touch, and to ask before it guesses.

#### Get started with Sourdough

Install the starter, bake a raw PHP app, fetch WayneUI, serve it, and check the label on the jar.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer bake a new app with Sourdough, the app starter of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Sourdough 0.1 bakes one shape, raw PHP on WayneUI's standalone path, with SESAME (sign-in), HELMET (security headers and the /up check), PROCTOR (checks), the Preflight CI components and Squire's Citadel deploy files already in it.

Read first:
- https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of Sourdough's pages, each one as Markdown; llms-full.txt beside it holds the README too. Fetch what you need; do not work from memory.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: get_project_status and read_project_docs for sourdough answer from the stack's own docs, and policy_lookup gives today's PHP support from CREED. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt

Task:
1. Check that PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer are on the PATH, and say which versions you found.
2. Install the starter with `composer global require waynestate/sourdough`. If the sourdough command is then not found, add the folder that `composer global config bin-dir --absolute` prints to the PATH.
3. Bake the app with `sourdough new my-app --raw`, using the folder name I give you in place of my-app, and change into it.
4. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once. Windows (PowerShell): `curl.exe -o public/wayne-ui.php https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/wayne-ui/-/raw/main/php/standalone/wayne-ui.php`. macOS and Linux: `curl -o public/wayne-ui.php https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/wayne-ui/-/raw/main/php/standalone/wayne-ui.php`.
5. Run `composer install`, then `php -S localhost:8000 -t public`, and tell me to open http://localhost:8000. Locally SESAME signs in with its fake driver.
6. Run `sourdough manifest --check` in the app and report what it says.

Constraints:
- Only the raw PHP shape bakes in Sourdough 0.1. The Laravel and Vue flags print a plan and stop with exit 1; never say they made an app. For Laravel with Inertia and Vue, WELD is the finished app: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt
- .sourdough/manifest.json records every file Sourdough wrote. Managed files are Sourdough's; .env.example and README.md are seeded and mine. Commit the manifest.
- The deploy files (build.sh, scripts/release.sh, the .squire/ config) come from Squire. Never edit them by hand.
- Never commit .env, and never paste a secret into a prompt or a file.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess: a folder name, a PHP version you cannot read, or anything that touches a deploy.

Output: what you ran and what it said, the app's files one level deep, then your questions.
```

#### Check what has drifted in a Sourdough app

Read the manifest, list the managed files that changed, and propose what to put back, before anything is fed.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent checking an app that Sourdough baked, at Wayne State University. Sourdough is the app starter of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Every app it bakes carries .sourdough/manifest.json: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers chosen, and a sha256 hash of every file it wrote, each marked managed or seeded.

Read first:
- https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then llms-full.txt beside it: the README's manifest section says what managed and seeded mean.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for sourdough and squire, and run_proctor_check for this app. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.
- .sourdough/manifest.json, composer.json and public/index.php in this app.

Task:
1. Run `sourdough manifest --check` at the app's root. Exit 0 is clean, 1 means a managed file changed or is missing, 2 is a tool error.
2. For each file it reports, say what changed, as far as you can tell, and whether it looks deliberate.
3. If ADVISOR is connected, call run_proctor_check for this app and list the findings.
4. Change nothing. For each drifted file, propose whether to put it back or keep the change, and why.

Constraints:
- Seeded files (.env.example and README.md) are mine and never count as drift.
- The deploy files come from Squire, through Sourdough. Never hand-edit them to make a check pass.
- sourdough feed, which will bring template updates in, is not built yet. Do not promise it.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything that deploys.

Output: a table (file, managed or seeded, state, deliberate or not), the PROCTOR findings, then your proposals and your questions.
```

The agent reads the same pages you do: [llms.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them all in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). Nothing here phones home; the buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked. The agent can knead, but you decide when the loaf is ready to bake.
